Beyond the wall of the forest, between branches decorated with countless leaves, could be seen the faint glow of a wheat field dancing in the moonlight. The full moon shone on the vacant night, filling the unnaturally lit world with strange shadows. Here, however, the great oaks above shielded the loamy floor from visibility. Every step he took was laced with caution against wild roots and stones that wished to acquaint him with the ground. His path was familiar to him though, and he was confident in his own ability.

The scattering sound of small animals, a distant bubbling creek, and an amateur chorus of insects accompanied him on his midnight strolls. He found calmness in the concealing nighttime that was foreign to the morning. When he could afford it, he spent many hours of the deep night wandering the sleeping earth, so that he was accustomed to its voice. Tonight, he heard another voice.

It came from deep in the woods; a hushed voice strained to make its way to him through rustling leaves. As he trekked quietly closer, he could discern multiple voices. A dull light glinted through the trees. He crept stealthily to the edge of a clearing. In its center, amidst sprouting grasses, a small table sat surrounded by four dull-grey silhouettes. A gloomy lantern lit what appeared to be a map sprawled out before them. He held his breath to better hear them.
“…you do?” asked one of the figures. 
“It would appear that we have unwanted company, friends.” a figure said calmly. The man’s heart felt as if it dropped into his stomach. He feared he should have ignored his curiosity.

“Agreed, brother. How do you propose we go about this unpleasantry?” This one spoke in a strange accent he didn’t recognize. Part of him wanted to flee, but a greater part of him stood solidified in a contradictory combination of intrigue and fear.
“Well, I suggest “

“Pick up that rock.” The final figure suggested.

“What? No, shut up, Derek.” said the calm voice, slightly out of character. “Ahem, now, we must investigate the area. An expansive searching spell should identify him quickly enough.”

Spell? He thought to himself. Just what had he wandered upon?

The accented voice said, “I concur. …Derek, are you in agreement?”

“I say we set the forest ablaze. That’ll get him.”

A silence consumed the party, followed quickly by a sigh from one of the members.

“Dang it, Derek, every time with you.” said the frustrated voice.

“What? Am I wrong? That’ll get him out and/or dispose of him. What do you want from me?”

“We are in the forest, Derek. Do you really want to set it on fire whilst we are in it?”

“We can’t be harmed by fire, you know that.” argued Derek.

“While you are technically correct, igniting the wood would prove too troublesome for us to realize the our plans.” explained the accented one.

“Excuse me, but whom out ranks whom here?”

“We don’t have ranks, and I don’t think you’re using that word right.”

“I have gasoline.”

The three continued on about the best course of action for them to take, while the fourth figure remained silent. Fragments of moonlight shifted in and out of existence on the forest floor about the ghostly group. The man stood still watching this strange discussion unfold. He felt no danger in the midst of their incompetence. He moved silently around the clearing to find a better view. All he could gather is that their faces were covered by deep hoods.

“Excuse me; it appears the figure has changed positons.” announced the other figure.

“Great. Now he might be out of range. Derek, can we please just decide on what to do here? Who knows if this will get in the way.” said the aggravated voice.

“We could pick up that rock.”

“Forget the rock. Look, you have to decide what to do here, but we agreed we have to be in agreement. Just cast the spell.”

Derek was silent for a moment, lost in contemplative thought. “We could cast the searching spell on the rock. Then we don’t have to lift it.”

“What do you think is under that rock? Worms? Do you want worms, Derek?”

Derek then explained, “How do you think that rock got here? Look around you. See any other rocks? No? That’s because there aren’t any. Somebody put that rock here. Rocks like that one don’t just happen upon a forest like this one. Where would it have come from? You think a bird dropped it? A coconut, maybe, but not a rock. I guarantee something powerful is under that rock.”

“Fine. Whatever. You okay with lifting the rock?” said the defeated voice to the accented one.

“I suppose.”

“Yes. Yes. I cast the searching spell on the rock.” commanded Derek.

“Well?” asked the curious voice, “What is it?”

“Worms.”

“Screw you, Derek.”

“Hey, these worms might make a powerful potion.”

“We can use them in tequila. How does that help us?”

“More fuel to burn down the forest. This has got to be fate.”

“Darn it, Derek! Every time with you.” complained not-calm-anymore voice, “Every time it’s a rock, or a tree, or a looking for a fish in a puddle in the middle of the freaking road because you think if you save it it will have to grant you a wish.”

“Yeah, a wish fish.”

“This is why nobody loves you.”

A curious breeze breathed through the trees. The man was sitting now, thoroughly amused by the situation that had unfolded. The most silent of the group was resting is hand against his head. He appeared to be asleep. The accented man was silent too, with his arms folded and head resting on his chest. The first glimmer of dawn was bleeding across the horizon.

The disheveled voice looked up. “Great. Just great, Derek. Now we have to wait another month for the full moon to play again. We’ve accomplished nothing.”

“We know someone is missing a rock. There might be a reward for it.”

Yellow-green sunlight filtered by leaves beat down upon the table and its occupants. The moment the dusty beams reached them, they disappeared. The man blinked hard from his spot among the growth. He hadn’t expected that. He stood tall, reaching his arms high above his head to stretch out the stiffness. He made his way to what he could now identify as a large stone table, nearly tripping on a hidden rock on the way. On the table was a large D&D map, the many dice and character pieces sprawled about. He wasn’t at all sure what to make of this. Certainly this was their hell, being cursed to play with that Derek for all eternity.

He had what he considered a novel idea. He went back to retrieve the rock, and placed it square on the center of the map. That will makes things interesting next month, thought the man.
